summary:
Deep-space missions face a critical medical challenge: extreme distances cause severe communication delays and signal blackouts, leaving astronauts without real-time support during emergencies. We built a continuous health monitoring system that leverages Starlink’s low-Earth orbit satellite network to keep astronauts connected to Earth with minimal latency.
​Our platform combines a live biometric dashboard, tracking heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, suit metrics, and radiation, with contactless computer vision. Using onboard cameras, the system scans facial micro-expressions and blink rates to detect fatigue, stress, or hypoxia early without bothering the crew.
​To make this mission-ready, we designed a clear hardware roadmap integrating medical wearables, edge microcontrollers, and encrypted onboard storage to prevent critical data loss. Built for long-duration missions like Artemis, our system gives Mission Control instant, reliable health data to intervene rapidly before a minor issue becomes life-threatening.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Deep space missions face severe communication delays and signal dropouts, leaving astronauts isolated during emergencies. We built a continuous health monitoring system using Starlink low-latency satellite network to keep crews connected to Earth in real time. The platform combines a live telemetry dashboard tracking heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, suit metrics, and radiation with contactless computer vision. Using onboard cameras, the system scans facial micro expressions and blink rates to detect fatigue, stress, or hypoxia early without bothering the crew.

​What benefits does it have?

Our system ensures continuous, uninterrupted medical tracking and prevents communication blackouts during critical space operations, keeping astronauts safe and fully connected.

​What is the intended impact of the project?

Built for long duration missions like Artemis, our project empowers Mission Control with instant, reliable health data so they can intervene rapidly before minor issues become life-threatening.

​What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We built the web application using React and Vite, and powered it with Capacitor to run smoothly as a cross platform app. We also integrated Starlink connectivity, medical wearables, edge microcontrollers, and encrypted onboard storage.

​How is your project creative? What factors did your team consider?

Our project stands out through its non-intrusive monitoring approach, using contactless vision to track fatigue and stress without bothering the crew. We carefully considered crew comfort, low-latency satellite data transfer, and zero-data-loss architecture under extreme space conditions.
